papers.title_in_file: NARMA10 Univariate Time Series Forecasting: Device: Emucore
papers.version_note: Web page text of a QCi notebook tutorial; no page breaks in the text layer, read as one page.
papers.what_it_is: A QCi tutorial notebook that forecasts the NARMA10 series with the EmuCore reservoir computing device and a linear readout.

assertions.value: The authors state that EmuCore, developed by QCi, is an electronic reservoir computing platform designed for complex time series forecasting tasks.
assertions.anchor: Web page, section Reservoir computing with EmuCore
quotes: EmuCore, developed by QCi, represents a cutting-edge electronic reservoir computing platform designed specifically for tackling complex time series forecasting tasks.

assertions.value: The page calls EmuCore QCi's photonic reservoir emulator in its contents list.
assertions.anchor: Web page, introduction, notebook organization list
quotes: We will be utilzing QCi's photonic reservoir emulator EmuCore.
assertions.reader_inference: The same page calls EmuCore an electronic reservoir platform in its own section; the two descriptions differ and the page does not reconcile them.

assertions.value: The authors state that the reservoir maps input signals from their original values to a higher dimensional feature space.
assertions.anchor: Web page, section Reservoir computing with EmuCore
quotes: The reservoir maps input signals from their original values to a higher dimensional feature space.

assertions.value: The page refers readers to a QCI paper at arXiv 2102.09049 for the reservoir architecture, and says EmuCore uses a time delayed reservoir architecture.
assertions.anchor: Web page, section Reservoir computing with EmuCore
quotes: utilizing a time delayed reservoir architecture
see this paper from QCI at https://arxiv.org/pdf/2102.09049.pdf

assertions.value: The page defines the NARMA10 benchmark by a recurrence with coefficients 0.3, 0.05, 1.5 and 0.1, with the input drawn uniformly from the interval 0 to 0.5.
assertions.anchor: Web page, section Create NARMA10 time series
quotes: we will utilze a common forecasting benchmark NARMA10
is drawn from a uniform distribution in the interval [ 0 , 0.5 ]
assertions.certainty_reason: The page states the benchmark definition it uses.
assertions.reader_inference: The recurrence is printed in the page text with a sum over nine lags (i = 0 to 9).

assertions.value: The authors describe NARMA 10 as a synthetic generator that mimics real-world processes by producing nonlinear and chaotic patterns.
quotes: NARMA 10 is a synthetic time series generator that mimics the behavior of real-world processes by generating nonlinear and chaotic patterns.
assertions.reader_inference: The page gives no evidence for the claim that the series is chaotic.

assertions.value: The authors use a NARMA10 series of size 1000, with 800 samples for training and 200 for testing, generated with seed 0.
assertions.anchor: Web page, section Create NARMA10 time series, In [2]
quotes: Let us consider a NARMA10 series of size 1000 with 800 samples in the training portion and 200 in the testing portion.
dataset = NARMA10(seed= 0 , train_size=TRAIN_SIZE, test_size=TEST_SIZE)
assertions.certainty_reason: The page states the data split and seed it ran.

assertions.value: The authors configure the reservoir with vbias 0.31, gain 0.72, 400 nodes and 400 taps, and process data with feature scaling 0.1 and density 1.0.
assertions.anchor: Web page, section Modelling data using reservoir, In [6] and In [7]
quotes: VBIAS = 0.31 GAIN = 0.72 NUM_NODES = 400 NUM_TAPS = 400
FEATURE_SCALING = 0.1 DENSITY = 1.0
assertions.certainty_reason: The page states the settings of its own run.

assertions.value: The page defines vbias and gain as parameters in the range 0 to 1, num_nodes as the number of hidden nodes in a single hidden layer, and num_taps as the number of connections, which should generally be set to less than the number of nodes.
assertions.anchor: Web page, section Modelling data using reservoir
quotes: vbias: bias to apply to each node in reservoir range for parameter [0,1].
num_nodes: the total number of hidden nodes to instantiate within the reservoir, a single hidden layer.
num_taps: number of connections in reservoir, generally should be set to less than the number of nodes in reservoir.
assertions.reader_inference: The example sets num_taps equal to num_nodes (400 each), which is not less than the number of nodes as the guidance suggests.

assertions.value: The page describes gain as a memory setting for how long inputs affect the reservoir, in the range 0 to 1.
assertions.anchor: Web page, section Modelling data using reservoir
quotes: gain: memory setting for system how long should inputs effect reservoir similar to beta in adaptive gradient descent range for parameter [0,1].

assertions.value: The authors state that the client must acquire a device lock before use, that the lock call waits indefinitely until the lock is available, and that the lock is released after processing so other users can access the reservoir.
assertions.anchor: Web page, section Modelling data using reservoir, In [5] and In [8]
quotes: The above function will wait indefinitely until the device lock is avaialble.
Once finished processing it is important to release the lock so that other users can access the reservoir computer
assertions.reader_inference: Access is exclusive and serial: one user at a time per device.

assertions.value: The authors train a simple linear regression model on the reservoir response to predict the NARMA10 target.
assertions.anchor: Web page, section Train prediction model, In [10]
quotes: we can build a simple linear regression model using the reservoir response as its input.
assertions.certainty_reason: The page states the readout it used.

assertions.value: The authors report a train mean squared error of 0.0001, train R-squared 0.99, test mean squared error 0.0003, test R-squared 0.96, train NRMSE 0.09582885843850779 and test NRMSE 0.19772048772699802 for the EmuCore reservoir with a linear readout on NARMA10.
assertions.anchor: Web page, section Evaluate predictions, In [12] output
quotes: Train Mean Squared Error: 0.0001 Train R-squared: 0.99 Test Mean Squared Error: 0.0003 Test R-squared: 0.96 Train NRMSE: 0.09582885843850779 Test NRMSE: 0.19772048772699802
assertions.reader_inference: One run, one seed, 800 training and 200 test samples; no repeat, no error bar and no baseline appears on the page. The test NRMSE is about twice the train NRMSE.

assertions.value: The page defines NRMSE as the root mean squared difference between estimate and target divided by the standard deviation of the target.
assertions.anchor: Web page, section Evaluate predictions, In [11]
quotes: def NRMSE ( target, estimate ): return np.sqrt(((estimate - target) ** 2 ).mean()) / np.std(target)
assertions.certainty_reason: The page gives the NRMSE code it ran.

assertions.value: The authors state that using a reservoir allows simpler models to obtain higher accuracy than is possible without this data augmentation approach.
assertions.anchor: Web page, section Train prediction model
quotes: Utilzing a reservoir allows for simpler models to obtain higher accuracy than is possible without this data augmentation approach
assertions.reader_inference: The page runs no comparison with a model that lacks the reservoir, so the page does not support this statement with its own result.
